subject: DPA - evidence chain for certified deletion & regional fallback flow
body:
From: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@acmecorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on DPA deletion evidence chain and fallback hosting

Olga / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo. Legal has a couple of follow-ups on the deletion language and how we get proof back to them if a deletion request is initiated across multiple geo-placements. High-level asks:
- What operational evidence do you provide to certify deletion (logs, certificate, timeline)?
- If processing is routed to a fallback region (e.g., EU->US) during capacity events, how is residency recorded and reported?

We’re trying to map this into our procurement checklist. Matt

--
Matt Reynolds
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Payments

----
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@acmecorp.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion evidence chain and fallback hosting

Matt — thanks for the list. I captured answers below and attached a short playbook for your legal team (redwood-certified-erasure-playbook.pdf).

1) Certified deletion evidence we can provide:
   - Deletion execution record (timestamped job id + operator id)
   - Immutable audit entry (sha256 of job metadata) stored in our compliance ledger
   - Snapshot of storage index changes indicating tombstone/rewrite with object ids
   - Optional certificate of erasure (signed PDF) that references DocuSign envelope id for contract traceability

2) Residency & fallback recording:
   - Routing policy is deterministic per-request; if we fallback to a different region we append a routing trace to the request metadata and mark the session as geofallback="true"
   - For account-level residency (your ship-to region = EU), we only use fallback for compute; persisted storage remains in-region unless you opt-in to cross-region replication for DR
   - We capture and return the full routing trace in the erasure report so you can see where processing occurred and where data was deleted

3) Timing expectations:
   - Primary deletion job completes within the contractual erase-window (default 30 days for backups; can be shortened in redline)
   - For cross-region backup wipe we include a verification window (up to 10 days) to allow for consistency across replicas

Next steps: I’ve suggested a redline for the DPA language around evidence (attached dpa-redlines-ACME-4492.docx). Can your legal team indicate whether a signed certificate is sufficient vs. direct ledger access?

Thanks,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Compliance

Olga — quick clarifying Q from our counsel (Claire is copied):

Claire: is the "certificate" generated by Redwood human-readable with verifiable references (job id, timestamps, hash), and can we get an API endpoint to pull the verification blob? Also, if a fallback compute event occurred, would the certificate reflect that?

Legal will want the certificate to stand on its own for audit purposes.

Regards,
Acme Legal

----
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>, matt.reynolds@acmecorp.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion evidence chain and fallback hosting

Hi Claire / Acme team — quick answers:

- The certificate is a signed, human-readable PDF that includes: deletion job id, ISO timestamps (UTC), list of object ids affected, SHA256 digest of the job metadata, and a reference to the ledger entry id. Example snippet attached in the playbook.
- We can offer a read-only verification API (tokenized) that returns the raw verification blob (json) for an envelope id. That blob includes routing_trace: ["eu-west-1","eu-west-1-cache","us-east-1-fallback"] when a fallback happened.
- If you prefer ledger push, we can push an anchored proof to a merchant-owned S3 or to your SIEM via secure webhook (mutually agreed format).

Operational caveat: when backup replicas are purged across regions we introduce a short proof propagation window (typically 48–168 hours) while replicas converge; the certificate will include a verification_status field set to PENDING until confirmation (we surface a final verification timestamp once all replicas report deletion).

If that window is a blocker, we can add an SLA clause to shorten propagation to X days for an extra commitment.

Best,
Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Dupont <c.dupont@eu-tek.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@acmecorp.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA deletion evidence chain and fallback hosting

Thanks for the fast turn here. A couple of final asks from our audit team before we proceed to signature:
- Can Redwood add a short paragraph to the DPA (suggested language below) that explicitly states: "A certificate of erasure will include a routing trace and the verification_status for all replicas at time of issuance."
- Requesting an example verification API response (anonymized) to attach to the contract as an appendix.

Suggested sentence (for discussion):
"Upon completion of an erasure request, Redwood will issue a signed Certificate of Erasure that contains the deletion job identifier, timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC, the list of affected object identifiers, a cryptographic digest of the job metadata, and a routing trace that identifies any cross-region processing. The Certificate includes a verification_status field indicating whether replica purges are pending or confirmed and will be updated in the verification log when propagation completes."

If you can accept language and a sample API response, legal should be able to move quickly.

Claire

--
Claire Dupont
Senior Counsel (Europe) — External Audit Liaison
EU-Tek (audit partner for Acme)
